title: The Spine
question: Which part of the spine is it?
lines: Seven small bones hold up your head. Which part of the spine?
Watch the glowing section at the top of the spine.
Which part of the spine is glowing?
The lumbar section is the low back, with larger bones.
The seven glowing vertebrae are in the neck.
It's B. The cervical spine.
Why it matters: it lets your head nod, tilt and turn.

title: The Spine
question: How many bones are glowing?
lines: The low back carries the most weight. How many bones is it?
Watch the glowing section of the lower spine.
How many vertebrae are in the glowing section?
The neck has seven, and the rib-bearing mid-back has twelve.
The lumbar spine, in the low back, usually has five of the biggest.
It's C. Five.
Why it matters: big vertebrae carry much of your upper body's weight.

title: The Spine
question: Which section of the spine is it?
lines: Twelve vertebrae in your spine each carry a pair of ribs.
Watch the glowing section in the middle of the back.
Which section of the spine is it?
The lumbar section is lower and has bigger bones.
The glowing section is the upper and middle back.
It's D. The thoracic spine.
Why it matters: it forms the back of the rib cage.

title: The Spine
question: What are the top two vertebrae?
lines: The top of your spine has two specially named bones.
Watch the two small glowing bones at the top of the spine.
What are the top two vertebrae?
The sacrum and coccyx are at the very bottom.
Atlas is C1 and holds up the head. Axis is C2.
It's A. Atlas and axis.
Why it matters: together they let your head nod and turn.

title: The Spine
question: How many vertebrae form the sacrum?
lines: One bone at the base of your spine was once separate pieces.
Watch the glowing triangle at the bottom of the spine.
How many vertebrae form the sacrum?
The neck has seven vertebrae, but they stay separate.
The sacrum forms from five vertebrae that fuse together.
It's A. Five.
Why it matters: the sacrum forms the back wall of the pelvis.
